newsitem.title: CANADA: Reynolds and Quebec in mill joint-venture.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds and Quebec in mill joint-venture.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co and Quebec government-owned Societe generale de financement (SGF) said on Tuesday they agreed to form a joint venture to operate Reynolds' rolling mill in Cap-de-la-Madeleine, Quebec and its coil coating facility in Toronto.
Reynolds and SGF each would have a 50 percent interest in the joint venture, which is expected to be completed in the third quarter. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

SGF said Reynolds' rolling mill was a leader in the rapidly growing market for aluminum brazing and plain finstock used in automotive air conditioning and radiators, as well as aluminum foil for the packaging industry.
The mill also produces building sheet, utensil coil and other industrial aluminum products. The plant employs about 700 people.
The coil coating plant in Toronto is a specialized custom coater of aluminum coil and employs approximately 50 people.

SGF's investment in the joint venture would provide the basis for a major capital program at the rolling mill aimed at increasing slab homogenizing capacity, coil size and quality, and light gauge rolling and finishing capacity, the agency said.
The joint venture will obtain independent bank financing and will be independently managed, with Reynolds and SGF having equal representation on its board.

Completion of the transaction was subject to due diligence, negotiation and execution of definitive agreements, obtaining financing, and board approvals as required by the respective organizations, SGF said.
